title: Michel Le Tellier to Pierre de Marca, 26 April 1644, BnF Baluze 103 f. 50r-v (DECODE R2742), in the Le Tellier-Marca cipher of 1644

documents.shelfmark: BnF Baluze 103 f. 50r-v (Gallica btv1b9001389d views 111-112); DECODE R2742

plaintext.source: No period decipherment of f. 50 in the volume (contributor's search of all 743 views); the 1921 Baluze catalogue's 'avec traductions' holds for the four sister letters ff. 171, 189, 200, 230 only.

transcription.source: Gallica / BnF IIIF full-size scans (4864x6996), views 111-112
transcription.notes: Contributed (Harumi-Matsuba, issue #54): Claude transcription corrected against five OpenAI Codex passes; a sixth independent Codex pass agrees on 568/626 sign names (90.7%). No human check. 626 = sign tokens of the 32 lines (--measure --drop-first); measure.py counts 619 cipher units (clear words excluded, the code pair =11 =o as one). Spot-checked here on 9 lines (167 signs) against the IIIF image at 2400 px.

system.summary: Le Tellier-Marca cipher of 1644: a homophonic alphabet of figures 2-24, letters and invented signs, with overlined figures and letters for words and names (=3 de La Motte, =32 Barcelone, =11 =o la Reyne).

diacritics.note: A bar through a sign changes it (barred y = n, plain y = g; barred-tail mz = s, plain mi = i); an overline marks a code group.

system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's table, rebuilt from the four deciphered sister letters (ff. 171, 189, 200, 230 with decipherments ff. 172, 190, 205-206, 232); the contributor checked it on f. 230r against f. 232r.
system.notes: Several signs carry two values (6 = t or l, ff = a or d, 9 = r, s or i); the code numbers run alphabetically (9 pour, 11 que, 12 qui, 22 troupes, 26 vous).

prior_solution.where: NoAutopilot/cipher-lab ciphers/baluze103-letellier-marca-1644 (13 Oct 2026, 'Status: partial', 'Verdict: parked'): 451 of 630 signs valued with Tomokiyo's table, words such as conseil, que ledit, descouvert, surtout, no connected text. Tomokiyo lists f. 50 as undeciphered. DECODE R2742 carries the status Decrypted but no decryption text.

conditions.human_role: Contributed: a person chose the target and decided to publish; the transcription, key additions and reading were made by Anthropic's Claude (Claude Code, Opus 5.5) with OpenAI Codex second transcriptions. In this project: integration and spot-check only.

solution.what: Contributor (Harumi-Matsuba): Tomokiyo's 'Le Tellier-Marca Cipher (1644)' table (cryptiana louisxiv0.htm) rewritten with sign names; f. 230r lines 1-21 aligned by DP with its period decipherment f. 232r, 412 of 424 signs falling on a key value; values added (R = c, ff = d, 6 = l, =83 le Gouverneur ...).

Contributor: Claude transcribed f. 50r-v (32 lines) by sign name from full-size scans; five Codex passes used to correct it (all five agree on 572 of 626), corrections re-checked on enlarged crops; a sixth independent Codex pass agrees on 568/626 (90.7%).
Contributor: key applied and the reading joined; 14 of 32 lines marked sure, 18 with letters supplied or a sign chosen from context; nine signs or code groups without a value.
Contributor: real key vs 1000 shuffles of its values (French trigram score), 0/1000 at or above the real key, also with table values only, on the last fifth alone, and on each Codex transcription.
Contributor: blind calibration on f. 171r lines 12-24 against the period decipherment f. 172r (reading frozen and hashed before the answer was opened): 253/277 signs (91.3%), 337/360 letters (93.6%).

Contributor: all 743 views of Baluze 103 checked; period decipherments found for ff. 171, 189, 200, 230, none for f. 50. HathiTrust and Internet Archive phrase searches: 0 hits; NoAutopilot's partial draft found.

Here (measure.py, own decoder): bare key decode scores -2.490/char on fr-1600-letters (order 5, no spaces), the joined reading -1.977; 200 shuffled keys median -5.087, max -4.500, 0/200 at or above the bare decode.

Here: DP alignment of each line's signs with the contributor's line reading: 600 of 619 cipher units (96.9%) carry a key value or code word that stands in the reading; their calibration recomputed from their files, 339/360 letters (94.2%, our normalisation).

Here: 9 lines (r01-r03, r17-r20, v01, v12; 167 signs) compared with the BnF IIIF image at 2400 px: sign count agrees on every line and no sign reads differently, except the 6/sigma choice and the double-barred cross before =3 on r19, which the contributor already flags. This is a second AI look (Claude), not a human check.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): f. 50: the contributor's transcription contributed/data/transcription_f50.txt, reading contributed/docs/READING.en.md and bare decode data/decoded_f50.txt; key contributed/data/key.tsv.
Verification 5 (plain-bar rows): the scored file was the bare decode; the contributor's joined French reading written out as f50_reading.md: plain 0.6, explicit 0.667. Keeps read at the bar.
Read bar applied per document (v10): 1 of 1 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5): independent decoder (verify_dudout_20261114.py) from key.tsv, transcription_f50.txt and the code groups of Tomokiyo's table (louisxiv0.htm) and METHOD.en.md: bare decode 725/725 letters equal to decoded_f50.txt. Reading side: 13 letters of the line readings come from no sign and are not in [ ], 9 of them the documented qu'il from an unbarred 12; 4 are silent supplies (pr[i]s s-, c[e] que v03, [d]'icy v04, p[a]ssent v06, the last checked on view 112). Open signs re-read on views 111-112: r02 p is the s of Tomokiyo's table; the dots of r04 also stand between plain letters; the mark of r06 23 stands over the 3 only; v05 18 carries a full bar, and its alphabetical slot between qui (12) and vous (26) fits sçavoir. v10 read_share 0.924 unchanged.

outcome.method_basis: Tomokiyo published the Le Tellier-Marca table of 1644 for this correspondence and named f. 50 as its one undeciphered letter; the contributor applied it, with additions checked on the sister letter f. 230r and its period decipherment.
outcome.fraction_read_source: measure.py: 600 of 619 cipher units of contributed/data/transcription_f50.txt whose key value or code word stands in the contributor's line reading (contributed/docs/READING.en.md), letters they supplied in [ ] and unread signs removed.
outcome.notes: Contributed, AI-only (Claude transcription, Codex cross-checks), no human check of the transcription. The calibration on f. 171r (91.3% of signs) means about one sign in eleven may be misread; 18 of 32 lines rest on context. Graded read in part until a person checks the signs against the image.

texts.label: Baluze 103 f. 50r-v, 26 April 1644 (DECODE R2742), contributed reading (Harumi-Matsuba, issue #54)
texts.summary: Michel Le Tellier, secretary of state for war, warns Pierre de Marca, newly arrived in Barcelona as visitor general in Catalonia, that the Barcelona councillors chose for his lodgings the house of a friend of Marshal de La Motte, who hoped in that way to learn everything Marca does and writes; Barcelona's agent at court complains that the Catalans' packets are opened at La Motte's, and the Queen wishes Marca to watch this, report and stop it. Reading contributed by Harumi-Matsuba with Tomokiyo's key, AI-made and not yet checked by a person.

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (1644 French: plain share is a bar too): the sweep scored the contributor's bare decode, contributed/data/decoded_f50.txt (line-labelled unspaced letter runs: plain 0.0, explicit 1.0), not a reading. Their joined French reading (contributed/docs/READING.en.md) copied alone as f50_reading.md: plain 0.6 (9/15), explicit 0.667 (10/15), hole rate 0.091. At the bar: the failing sentences carry the open signs (⟨22⟩, ⟨23̂⟩, ⟨‡‡⟩, ⟨=18⟩), the endings supplied in [ ], and the name Marca. Keeps read, with the standing caveat that the transcription was made and checked by AI only (NOTES.md: a person should check views 111-112).
